rules.plain_language_rule: Functional screening is used to observe broader movement capability.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Local ROM testing is used to investigate more specific joint-level movement limitations.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Dynamic testing assesses movement control and joint performance under more demanding conditions.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Screening findings should guide targeted exercise selection rather than generic corrective programmes.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: The system should distinguish mobility, stability/control, strength, asymmetry, and pain-related findings where possible.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Left and right sides should be recorded separately when the test permits.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Corrective exercises should be linked directly to the limitation they are intended to address.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Every corrective intervention should have a planned reassessment point.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Screening results are decision-support information, not medical diagnoses.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Pain or concerning clinical findings should trigger referral rather than automated corrective programming.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Tuck-jump and shoulder-stabilisation testing should be stored as dynamic movement assessments, separate from static ROM measures.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: The system should track whether movement quality changes over time, not merely whether a player once passed or failed a screen.
rules.domain: Movement Screening

rules.plain_language_rule: Coaches may administer functional and ROM tests within their training scope.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Medical care, injury diagnosis, and pain management remain the responsibility of qualified medical professionals.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Pain during screening should exit the automated corrective pathway and trigger appropriate referral.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: A multidisciplinary approach between coaching and medical staff is preferred where available.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Hip internal and external rotation should be assessed separately and bilaterally.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Hip ROM should be measured with a standardized protocol; goniometric measurement is preferable to rough visual estimation.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Course reference values for hip rotation should be treated as contextual reference ranges, not universal diagnostic thresholds.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Hip ROM findings should be interpreted alongside pain, asymmetry, sport demands, and athlete history.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Restricted hip rotation may influence movement quality and may be associated with groin, low-back, or adductor problems, but it does not by itself diagnose or predict injury.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Corrective exercises should be matched to the specific direction of restriction.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Corrective exercise should be followed by reassessment to determine whether ROM or movement quality has improved.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice

rules.plain_language_rule: Failure to improve, worsening symptoms, or pain should trigger review rather than simply increasing corrective volume.
rules.domain: Hip ROM and Scope of Practice
